title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in 'Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques)' (1986), Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic, combinatorial notion of 'models of shapes', starting in dimension 1. A 'modèle de 1-forme' (1-segment) is a set L with a family of segments I, each with an underlying set Ĩ, an interior I° and a boundary ∂I made of two points. The previous page fixes an 'origin' x0 in ∂L = {x0, x1}. It defines [x0,x] as {x0} if x = x0, as L if x = x1, and as Ĩ_{x0,x} otherwise. It then sets x ≤ y iff [x0,x] ⊂ [x0,y] (equivalently, x ∈ [x0,y]), and shows this is a partial order.

This page continues as follows.
(1) The order has least element x0 and greatest element x1.
(2) The order recovers the whole segment structure. Segments correspond bijectively to pairs {x,y} with x < y, via Ĩ_{x,y} = {z ∈ L | x ≤ z ≤ y} and ∂I_{x,y} = {x,y}.
(3) The order is 'infinitely divisible', i.e. dense: if x < y there is z with x < z < y.
(4) Added between the lines: the order is locally filtrant increasing and decreasing ('locally bifiltrant'). If x < y1, y2, there is y with x < y ≤ y1, y2, and dually.
(5) Converse, completed on the next page. A set with a dense order, distinct least and greatest elements, and local bifiltrance defines a 1-segment structure with ∂L = {x0, x1}.

The next page notes that swapping x0 and x1 replaces the order by its opposite. Density and local bifiltration are self-dual. So an unoriented segment structure is equivalent to a 'bi-order' (a pair of mutually opposite orders) satisfying these conditions.

Purpose: an order-theoretic, topology-free characterization of the 1-dimensional model (the 'tame' segment). It is the base case for building higher-dimensional combinatorial models of shapes, in the spirit of the tame topology called for in Esquisse d'un programme. The margin note '* Mais pour que ... il faut ∀a ∈ I ... ∃ ...' and a bottom-left 'F3)' suggest an extra condition or axiom was felt to be needed for the converse.
errors: Possible gap in the converse (order ⇒ segment model). Grothendieck works with a partial order and replaces totality by 'local bifiltrance'. But density, distinct endpoints and local bifiltrance do not force the order to be total. Counterexample (an 'eye' poset): x0 < chain L = Q∩(0,1/3), followed by two incomparable copies B, C of Q∩(1/3,2/3), followed by a chain U = Q∩(2/3,1), then x1. It is dense, has min and max, and is locally filtrant both ways, because L has no max and U has no min. Yet it is not a chain, and its 'segment' [x0,x1] is circle-like rather than segment-like. Unless the earlier segment axioms (not visible here) force comparability, the converse needs an extra hypothesis such as totality. The cramped marginal note 'Mais pour que ... il faut ...' plausibly records this worry.

Without a completeness condition the characterization pins down only a dense order with endpoints, not a topological arc (e.g. Q∩[0,1] qualifies). This is presumably intended (a 'tame', non-Archimedean-friendly setting) rather than an error.
The degenerate one-point case (Card L = 1) must be excluded or treated separately, as the next page notes.

ideas.what: Choosing an endpoint of a segment-structure induces an order with min and max from which segments are recovered as closed intervals
ideas.modern_name: Order/betweenness characterization of the segment; closed intervals of a bounded poset

ideas.what: Density ('infiniment divisible') plus local filtrance/cofiltrance as the axioms of a segment, using a partial rather than a total order
ideas.modern_name: Dense bounded poset with directedness conditions; compare dense linear orders with endpoints (Cantor) and the o-minimal base structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cantor (dense linear orders); o-minimality: van den Dries 1984, Pillay–Steinhorn 1986

ideas.what: An unoriented segment equals a 'bi-order', i.e. a pair of mutually opposite orders, with the axioms self-dual under reversal
ideas.modern_name: Betweenness relation / order up to reversal

ideas.what: Combinatorial/axiomatic 'models of shapes' as a foundation for tame topology
ideas.modern_name: Tame topology, o-minimal structures, combinatorial models of stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (programmatic, Esquisse 1984); van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (programmatic only; this axiomatics is not published)

missed.claim: Grothendieck tries to characterize the 1-dimensional tame model (segment) purely order-theoretically, with a possibly non-total order constrained by density and local bifiltrance. This is the first brick of an unpublished axiomatics of 'formes topologiques'. The higher-dimensional continuation does not appear to have been worked out in the literature in this order-theoretic style.
missed.quote: Elle est localement filtrante croissante et localement filtrante décroissante ... (et loc. bifiltrante)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a poset-based foundation for tame topology, alternative to o-minimality, that could be compared with o-minimal dense orders and with combinatorial models of stratified spaces and exit-path categories. It is mainly of historical interest at the 1-dimensional level.

missed.claim: The axioms (dense order with distinct endpoints, no completeness) coincide with the base of o-minimal structures, developed in exactly the same years (1984–86). Grothendieck does not mention o-minimality, and the literature does not seem to compare his 'géométrie des formes' with it.
missed.quote: I muni d'une relation d'ordre divisible, ayant un plus petit élément x0 et un plus grand élément x1, définit ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: documents an independent route toward tame topology contemporaneous with van den Dries–Pillay–Steinhorn.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is an elementary order-theoretic reformulation of a segment, classical in content. Its interest is historical, as a step in Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatization of tame shapes, and in the slightly unusual choice of local bifiltrance instead of totality, which may leave a gap.
transcription_corrections: 'En effet, {+s'identifie à+} l'ensemble des segments [-...-] un des couples' should read roughly 'En effet, l'ensemble des segments s'identifie à [l'ensemble] des couples {x,y} tels que x<y, et vice versa à un tel segment I_{x,y} ...'.
In the set-builder for Ĩ_{xy}, the membership looks like 'z ∈ L', possibly overwritten from 'z ∈ I'.
'définit {+I_{a,y}+}' at the bottom: the superscript is 'I_{x,y}', and the sentence continues on the next page: 'définit une structure de modèle de 1-forme'.
The local filtrance insertion reads: 'si x<y1,y2 ∃ y tel que x<y≤y1,y2, et de même décroissante*'.
Interlinear scribbles near 'x<y' look like an attempted reformulation of density via interiors (e.g. 'z ∈ I°_{x,y}'), not 'z≠x, z≠y'.
The bottom-left margin contains 'F3)', apparently a reference to an axiom labelled F3, followed by quantifier fragments '∀a∈I ... ∃a∈I ...'.
